articles.headline: They Created a Cell That's Almost Alive. What to Do With It Now?

It is still far from a self-sustaining cell that any scientist could manufacture from prepared ingredients, but the technology could eventually make it easier to produce medicines, foods, and other items that could not otherwise be produced with ordinary biology. The researchers working on SpudCell hope that it will eventually be a platform for biotechnology that will allow a simple cell to be engineered in scores of useful ways. SpudCell could potentially be misused, so its researchers are taking security seriously from the start - its DNA and proteins are engineered so that it can only survive on an exotic diet of chemicals not found in nature.

articles.headline: GhostMap: The Android flaw that crashes your phone before you open the app
articles.blurb: An APK entry using a nonstandard compression method slips past libziparchive's size check, while libandroidfw memory-maps it at its full declared size. As a result, any process that reads a malformed resource receives a SIGBUS. That flaw lets an app with no code or permissions trap system_server in a boot loop that only a factory reset clears, or cause its own icon to crash on every uninstall screen. Bitdefender found it when a packed banking dropper in the wild crashed its emulators, but the persistent boot loop was its own escalation. Google declined to ship a security fix even though the bug reproduces on Android 10 through 17. With no patch coming, defenders should flag APKs whose ZIP entries use compression methods other than stored or deflate before they're installed, since an on-device warning may come too late.

articles.headline: Escaping Firecracker from Guest Userspace
articles.blurb: Coinspect demonstrated a Firecracker sandbox escape from guest userspace. CVE-2026-122192 allowed a guest to read and modify live Firecracker VMM memory and gain code execution in the host-side process. The flaw stemmed from a failed memory replacement after a snapshot-backed RAM discard, leaving a stale KVM memory slot pointing to reused VMM memory. A second issue, FC-03, allowed VMM code to use io_uring to perform host operations blocked by seccomp, including sending a network message to a host listener. Firecracker v0.23.0 through v1.16.1 are affected. v1.16.2 and v1.17.0 fix the escape.

articles.headline: The SOC Files 5: Ghost in the pipeline, or a fileless SharePoint breach by Storm-2603
articles.blurb: Storm-2603 used the ONYPHE scanner to check a SharePoint server for ToolShell (CVE-2025-53770), waited three days, and on Christmas Eve loaded a webshell directly into IIS's w3wp.exe process memory. The webshell activated only for a specific User-Agent, tunneled into the internal network with suo5, escalated to SYSTEM using EfsPotato, and then moved to a vulnerable Velociraptor build, an EDR-killer driver, and a blocked Warlock ransomware attempt. Kaspersky attributed the intrusion with moderate confidence. Defenders should hunt for IIS paths that resolve in config but have no file on disk, which appear as IIS-Configuration ETW events 25 and 47 without the usual file-change monitoring events. Kaspersky has released CLRDeserializationExploitFinder to flag the deserialization exploit itself.

It shows each fix as a before-and-after dry-run plan, applies it, and reads every setting back to confirm. If encryption is already running, it can freeze the encryptor with SIGSTOP and capture its memory to recover keys. articles.blurb: Sectiv is a Burp Suite extension that runs captured proxy traffic past an LLM, guided by editable "skills" for IDOR, XSS, SQLi, and SSRF, and returns triaged findings with CVSS scores and HTML, Python, or curl PoCs. Testers can load two accounts to help the model reason about broken access control. It masks cookies, tokens, and JWTs before sending traffic to providers like OpenAI, Claude, DeepSeek, or a local Ollama model. Skills can be imported, exported, and tailored per target, and findings export to HTML, Markdown, or JSON for reporting.

articles.headline: Apple Will Scan Shared iCloud Links for Harmful Content, but Won't Explain What Counts as Harmful
articles.blurb: Apple will check photos and files shared via iCloud's “Anyone with the Link” setting for harmful content on iOS, iPadOS, and macOS 27.3. Publicly shared items lose end-to-end encryption, even with Advanced Data Protection enabled. Apple can remove files, block accounts, prevent re-registration, and contact law enforcement. It has not defined “harmful,” explained the screening method, said whether people review flags, or confirmed whether existing public links are covered.

articles.headline: OpenAI AI Pipeline Generates 948 Linux Root Escalation Exploits in 30-Hour Run
articles.blurb: OpenAI says an automated pipeline reproduced 1,724 Linux kernel vulnerabilities in 30 hours and generated 948 working local privilege-escalation exploits. The run produced 291 information-leak proofs of concept, patches for identified flaws, and at least 10 novel exploitation techniques. It cost $1.21 million in API credits, or $1,279 per exploit. OpenAI says unpatched systems with low-privileged access should be treated as accessible to well-resourced attackers with root access.

articles.headline: Bank Phishing Sites Show Fake ‘Suspended' Pages to Evade Takedowns
articles.blurb: Kela found more than 300 fake bank domains using a phishing kit that records visitor IP addresses. First visits receive bank login pages. The campaign targets business banking and treasury logins at 189 US institutions, with activity also seen in the UK, Australia, and New Zealand.

articles.headline: Cyberattack on Norway's aid agency may have swept up all user data
articles.blurb: Attackers used 27 compromised accounts to enter Norad's Grants Portal, potentially exposing names and email addresses for all 20,614 registered users, and also took applications and documents from three foreign organizations.

articles.headline: Chinese Nation-State Threat Activity Falls Sharply in Q2 and Q3 2026

articles.headline: AWS Security Hub now provides an SBOM inventory for your compute resources
articles.blurb: AWS Security Hub now shows an organization-wide inventory of the software packages installed across EC2 instances, ECR images, and Lambda functions, built from Amazon Inspector's SBOMs and queryable through the API, at no extra cost wherever Inspector is enabled.

articles.headline: Apple reportedly cuts employee AI budgets
articles.blurb: Apple is reportedly reducing employee allowances for third-party AI tools, with proposed daily caps of $100 for engineers and $25 for other staff. Some teams are also being encouraged to use cheaper or locally hosted models, although Apple hasn't confirmed the changes.

articles.headline: Microsoft expands unpublished Copilot Chat limits

articles.headline: What's new across Google's Agentic Data Cloud
articles.blurb: Google Cloud has announced major updates to its Agentic Data Cloud, introducing features like a borderless Lakehouse powered by Apache Iceberg, enhanced Knowledge Catalog context curation, and specialized infrastructure for scaling AI agents. These capabilities aim to give agents secure, real-time access to distributed enterprise data while lowering token costs and improving query performance. The announcements also include new development kits and integrated Gemini tools designed to assist both data practitioners and business users.

articles.headline: AI just raised the interest rate on your technical debt
articles.blurb: AI-assisted vulnerability discovery effectively raises the interest rate on technical debt by making exploits much cheaper and faster to develop. While finding bugs has become vastly accelerated, repairing them still moves at human speed, creating a dangerous asymmetry for organizations. Leadership teams should look into auditing deferred security tickets, sunsetting unused internet-facing systems, and reviewing accepted-risk registers on a regular schedule.

articles.headline: Who Checks the Boring Layer
articles.blurb: While high-profile security incidents often involve complex exploits, the underlying entry points frequently rely on basic vulnerabilities like missing access controls, unpatched firmware, and exposed credentials. articles.headline: Introducing MariaDB Enterprise Platform 2027: one foundation for the agentic enterprise
articles.blurb: MariaDB has introduced its Enterprise Platform 2027, a unified data foundation designed for AI agents and enterprise workloads. articles.headline: Confluent brings live SQL queries to streaming data
articles.blurb: Confluent made Lightning Tables generally available on AWS, letting applications query continuously updated Kafka data through SQL and APIs without maintaining a separate serving database. articles.headline: How to Use Test-Driven Development with AI Agents (Without Lowering Code Quality)

articles.headline: Want to Rent an Internet Address at the White House?

articles.headline: Tech Firms Dismantle Botnet That Turned 1.3M TV Boxes Into Proxies
articles.blurb: Google said today it worked with industry partners to dismantle a botnet made up of more than 1.3 million Android TV set-top boxes that ship with malicious software which secretly rents the user's Internet connection out to strangers and conducts advertising fraud. articles.headline: Widespread PHP Flaw May Cause Many Site Outages Today

articles.headline: U.K. Sanctions Cryptomus for RU Money Laundering

articles.headline: Microsoft Patches More Than 1,400 Security Flaws

articles.headline: FBI Arrests Executive at Ransomware Negotiation Firm
articles.blurb: Agents with the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) on Thursday arrested the co-founder of a Canadian cybersecurity firm in connection with an investigation into the ShinyHunters hacking group that recently relieved the FBI of sensitive data on thousands of agents, multiple sources tell KrebsOnSecurity.

articles.headline: ShinyHunters Extorted Boeing Spin-off Prior to Arrests
articles.blurb: A teenager from Amman, Jordan suspected of leading the prolific data theft and extortion group ShinyHunters has been detained and is reportedly cooperating with the FBI to identify other members of the hacking gang. KrebsOnSecurity has learned that the suspect, who uses the hacker handle "Rey," was detained as ShinyHunters was in the process of extorting a business unit recently divested by the global aerospace company Boeing, which manufactures the fleet of planes used by the employer of Rey's father -- Royal Jordanian Airlines.

articles.headline: Dutch Police Arrest ‘Reformed’ Hacker in Shiny Hunters Investigation
articles.blurb: Authorities in the Netherlands have arrested a 23-year-old convicted cybercriminal on suspicion of aiding in data thefts and extortions by the prolific hacker group ShinyHunters. articles.headline: ANC faces bruising defeat in South African local elections with 80% of ballots counted
articles.blurb: Former liberation movement’s share of national vote almost 14 percentage points below 2021 result The African National Congress is on course to suffer a bruising defeat in South Africa’s local elections, with the once dominant party of Nelson Mandela falling to under a third of the vote nationally with more than 80% of ballots counted. Wednesday’s fragmented vote marks another stage in the decline of the ANC, which has led national governments since the end of white minority apartheid rule in 1994. High unemployment, crime, corruption and poor local service delivery have all contributed to voters turning away from the party.

articles.headline: British healthcare worker with Ebola evacuated from DR Congo to UK
